# Data investigations - Practice Test - Year 7

Attempt all questions and show your working. Suggested time: 30 to 35 minutes.

## Section A: Consolidating (Questions 1-4)

**Question 1**

Which of these is a statistical question (one that is answered by collecting data that varies)?

(A) How old is my teacher?

(B) How many minutes do students in my class spend on homework each night?

(C) What is the capital city of Australia?

(D) How many legs does a spider have?

**Question 2**

A council wants to know how many hours residents spend in local parks each week. It surveys 200 of the town's 8000 residents.

(a) What is the population?

(b) What is the sample?

(c) What is the sample size?

**Question 3**

State whether each numerical variable is discrete or continuous.

(a) The number of cars passing the school gate in one minute

(b) The length of a lunch break, in minutes

(c) The mass of students' school bags

(d) The number of people living in each household

**Question 4**

Primary data is collected by you. Secondary data has already been collected by someone else. State whether each is primary or secondary data.

(a) Measuring the heights of the students in your class

(b) Using rainfall records downloaded from the Bureau of Meteorology website

## Section B: Standard (Questions 5-16)

**Question 5**

Write these stages of a statistical investigation in the correct order.

- Analyse the data
- Pose a question
- Interpret the results and communicate the findings
- Collect the data

**Question 6**

Jake wants to find out how many hours per week Year 7 students at his school spend playing sport. He surveys only the students at football training.

(a) Explain why his results are likely to be biased.

(b) Suggest a better way to choose his sample.

**Question 7**

A survey asks: "Don't you agree that the canteen food is too expensive?"

(a) Explain what is wrong with this question.

(b) Rewrite it as a fair question that collects numerical data.

**Question 8**

A school has 600 students. The principal wants a sample of 60 students to find how far students live from school. Which method gives the most representative sample? Explain.

(A) The first 60 students to arrive at school on Monday

(B) 60 names drawn at random from a list of all 600 students

(C) 60 students in the library at lunchtime

**Question 9**

To answer the question "How many minutes do Year 7 students spend on screens on a school night?", Priya asked 10 students. Their answers in minutes were:

$$45, \ 60, \ 90, \ 120, \ 60, \ 75, \ 30, \ 60, \ 150, \ 110$$

(a) Find the mean, median, mode and range.

(b) Write one sentence that answers Priya's question using your results.

**Question 10**

Choose the most suitable display, a dot plot or a stem-and-leaf plot, for each data set. Give a reason.

(a) The number of pets owned by each of 20 students (values from 0 to 4)

(b) The heights in centimetres of 25 students (values from 138 to 171)

**Question 11**

In a random sample of 50 Year 7 students, 18 walk to school. The school has 300 Year 7 students. Estimate how many Year 7 students at the school walk to school.

**Question 12**

You want to investigate whether Year 7 students can hold their breath for longer than Year 10 students.

(a) What variable will you measure, and in what units? Is it discrete or continuous?

(b) State one thing you would keep the same for every student to make it fair.

(c) How would you choose which students to test?

**Question 13**

Zara asked her 5 best friends whether they like basketball. All 5 said yes, so she concluded that every Year 7 student in Australia likes basketball. Give two reasons why her conclusion is not valid.

**Question 14**

A class investigated whether sleep affects reaction time. They measured reaction times, in seconds, for two groups.

| Group | Reaction times (seconds) |
|---|---|
| Slept 8 or more hours | 0.25, 0.28, 0.30, 0.27, 0.25 |
| Slept less than 6 hours | 0.32, 0.35, 0.30, 0.38, 0.35 |

(a) Find the mean reaction time for each group.

(b) What conclusion can the class make from this sample?

**Question 15**

A census collects data from every member of the population. For each situation, state whether a census or a sample is more suitable, and give a reason.

(a) Finding how long the batteries made by a factory last (testing a battery uses it up)

(b) Finding how many students in a class of 26 own a bike

(c) Finding the favourite TV show of Australian teenagers

**Question 16**

Twenty cars dropped students at school. The number of people in each car was recorded.

$$1, \ 2, \ 2, \ 1, \ 3, \ 4, \ 2, \ 1, \ 1, \ 2, \ 3, \ 2, \ 1, \ 5, \ 2, \ 1, \ 2, \ 3, \ 2, \ 1$$

(a) Copy and complete the frequency table.

| Number of people | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | | | | | |

(b) Find the mode.

(c) Find the total number of people and the mean number of people per car.

## Section C: Advanced (Questions 17-20)

**Question 17**

A student investigated the question "Do students who live further from school take longer to get there?" The data for 8 students is shown.

| Distance (km) | 1 | 2 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Travel time (min) | 5 | 8 | 10 | 12 | 15 | 18 | 20 | 32 |

(a) Find the mean distance and the mean travel time.

(b) Describe the relationship between distance and travel time.

(c) Give one limitation of this investigation.

**Question 18**

A random sample of 80 students from a school of 640 students was asked to name their favourite sport. $30\%$ of the sample chose soccer.

(a) How many students in the sample chose soccer?

(b) Estimate how many students in the whole school would choose soccer.

(c) Give one reason why the estimate might not be exact.

**Question 19**

A student grew bean plants with two fertilisers and measured their heights, in centimetres, after 3 weeks.

| Fertiliser | Heights (cm) |
|---|---|
| A | 12.5, 14.0, 13.5, 15.0, 13.0, 16.0 |
| B | 10.5, 12.0, 11.5, 13.0, 12.5, 12.5 |

(a) Find the mean and range for each fertiliser.

(b) Which fertiliser appears to work better? Explain.

(c) Give two things the student should do to make the conclusion more reliable.

**Question 20**

The six houses sold in a street last year sold for:

\$650 000, \$700 000, \$720 000, \$750 000, \$780 000, \$3 600 000

A real estate agent says, "The typical house in this street sells for \$1.2 million."

(a) Show how the agent got \$1.2 million.

(b) Find the median price.

(c) Explain why the median is a better measure of a typical price here.
answers_md:
# Data investigations - Answer Key

**Question 1**

Answer: (B)

**Question 2**

Answer: (a) All 8000 residents of the town (b) The 200 residents who were surveyed (c) $200$

**Question 3**

Answer: (a) Discrete (b) Continuous (c) Continuous (d) Discrete

**Question 4**

Answer: (a) Primary (b) Secondary

**Question 5**

Answer: Pose a question, collect the data, analyse the data, interpret the results and communicate the findings

**Question 6**

Answer: (a) Students at football training are likely to play more sport than other students, so the sample does not represent all Year 7 students. (b) Choose students at random from a list of all Year 7 students.

**Question 7**

Answer: (a) It is a leading question that pushes people to agree. (b) For example: "How much do you spend at the canteen in a usual week?"

**Question 8**

Answer: (B), because every student has an equal chance of being chosen; the other methods only include certain types of students.

**Question 9**

Answer: (a) Mean $80$ minutes ($800 \div 10$), median $67.5$ minutes, mode $60$ minutes, range $120$ minutes (b) For example: "A typical Year 7 student in the sample spends about 60 to 80 minutes on screens on a school night."

**Question 10**

Answer: (a) Dot plot, because there are only a few possible whole number values. (b) Stem-and-leaf plot, because there are many different values that can be grouped by tens.

**Question 11**

Answer: $108$ ($\frac{18}{50} \times 300$)

**Question 12**

Answer: (a) Time, in seconds; continuous (b) For example, use the same stopwatch and the same instructions, with every student sitting still (c) Choose a random sample of students from each year level, with the same number from each.

**Question 13**

Answer: The sample is far too small, and it is not representative (only her friends, who may share her interests), so the result cannot apply to all Year 7 students in Australia.

**Question 14**

Answer: (a) 8 or more hours: $0.27$ seconds; less than 6 hours: $0.34$ seconds (b) In this sample, students who slept more had faster (shorter) reaction times on average.

**Question 15**

Answer: (a) Sample, because testing every battery would use them all up (b) Census, because the class is small and easy to ask (c) Sample, because there are far too many teenagers to ask every one

**Question 16**

Answer: (a)

| Number of people | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 7 | 8 | 3 | 1 | 1 |

(b) $2$ (c) Total $41$ people, mean $2.05$ people per car ($41 \div 20$)

**Question 17**

Answer: (a) Mean distance $4 \text{ km}$ ($32 \div 8$), mean time $15$ minutes ($120 \div 8$) (b) Students who live further away generally take longer to travel to school. (c) For example, the sample is small, or students use different types of transport.

**Question 18**

Answer: (a) $24$ (b) $192$ ($30\%$ of $640$) (c) The sample may not exactly match the whole school, because a different random sample could give a different result.

**Question 19**

Answer: (a) A: mean $14.0 \text{ cm}$, range $3.5 \text{ cm}$; B: mean $12.0 \text{ cm}$, range $2.5 \text{ cm}$ (b) Fertiliser A, because its plants had a greater mean height. (c) For example, use more plants, and keep other conditions (sunlight, water, soil, pot size) the same for both groups.

**Question 20**

Answer: (a) The prices total \$7 200 000, and dividing by 6 gives a mean of \$1 200 000 (b) \$735 000 (c) The \$3 600 000 house is an outlier that pulls the mean up, so the mean is higher than five of the six prices; the median is not affected by one extreme value.
